newsitem.title: USA: Nike profits jump 24 pct; stock splits and soars.
newsitem.headline: Nike profits jump 24 pct; stock splits and soars.

text.p: Nike Inc., the world's biggest maker of athletic footwear, said Monday its earnings leaped by 24 percent in the latest quarter, and it further pleased Wall Street investors with news of a stock split, its second in as many years.
The Beaverton, Ore.-based company said it earned $226.1 million, or $1.53 a share, in its fiscal first quarter ended Aug. 31, compared with year-ago earnings of $182.1 million, or $1.25 a share.
Revenues jumped 34 percent to $2.28 billion from $1.70 billion last year.

Nike said its board of directors has approved a two-for-one stock split in both Nike Class A and Class B common shares in the form of a 100 percent stock dividend to be paid Oct. 23 to shareholders of record at the close of business Oct. 11.
Following the news, Nike's class B shares leaped $3.50 to $122.75 on the New York Stock Exchange.

"One year ago, we approved a two-for-one stock split. At that time, I cited the growing power of the Nike brand as strong evidence of our outstanding financial performance," said company Chairman Philip Knight.

"That brand strength, which many thought was nearing its peak last year, continues to grow unabated in fiscal 1997, propelling Nike to the best quarter in our history, record futures orders, and another stock split for our shareholders," he said.

In the first quarter, U.S. athletic footwear and apparel revenues totalled $1.35 billion, up a robust 39 percent from a year ago. International athletic footwear and apparel revenues rose 35 percent to $780.9 million, Nike said.

The company said worldwide orders for athletic footwear and apparel scheduled for delivery between September 1996 and January 1997, known as futures orders, were at a record $3.5 billion, 66 percent higher than for the same period last year.

"The strength of the Nike brand is clearly evident in the U.S. market where both our footwear and apparel are experiencing outstanding sell-through at retail," Knight said. "In footwear, our men's basketball business in the U.S. grew 48 percent in the first quarter, an exceptional number given our dominant position in that market."
"Nike's brand presence outside the U.S. market continues to develop dramatically," he said.

Nike's subsidiaries include Bauer Inc., the world's largest maker of hockey equipment; Cole Haan, a manufacturer of men's and women's dress and casual shoes and Sports Specialities Corp., a headwear manufacturer.
